lines.t: Tallow Ford smells of hot wax and wet stone. Candles burn in every window, though it is barely afternoon.
Beside the river, a woman is counting sheep. She counts them twice. She does not like the total.
The Hall's flag hangs at half-mast. Something here has gone badly wrong.
The smell hits first: smoke, mutton, and something worse. Goblins have turned an old quarry into a fortress of stolen furniture.
Somewhere inside, a hammer is ringing. It is not a smith's rhythm. It is a goblin hitting something it should not.
The Chief's enclosure is built from stolen doors. Dozens of them. Some still have their brass numbers.
A goblin the size of a barrel rises from a throne made of church pews. It wears a crown of bent spoons.
Salt-smell! Mark-smell! Hask said you would come sniffing. Hask said keep the chart. Hask said hit hard!
The Goblin Chief topples off his pew throne. The crown of spoons rolls away, ringing like a dropped pan.
Tucked in his belt is a waxed chart, folded small, with a red ring around a place called Reedhollow.
Hask's dig sites. All of them.
The marshes to the north are about to get a great deal more dangerous. Reeve Pask will want to hear of it.
